chapter_theme: The Bhairavi mantra (வயிரவி மந்திரம்): the goddess Bhairavi, also called Tripura and Manonmani, is a mantra of twelve kalas to be laid out, worshipped and recited with its rites, and she is the Shakti in whom the gods have their cause, who enters the devotee's heart, wakes him, takes away his deeds and births, and reveals Siva.
structure_note: The mantra's count of kalas and the lunar days of practice (1075 to 1080); her form and her worship in the lotus (1081 to 1087); the rites of the mantra, with breath, finger-placing, the limbs of the mantra, mudras and seed-letters (1088 to 1096); then a hymn of praise in which she enters the poet's heart (1097 to 1124). Each verse opens with the closing word of the one before, and the last verse returns to the twelve of the first.

1075.reading: Take Bhairavi as the first, with twelve kalas, conceive in her the letter A and maya, and with the twelve from the start and the fourteen at the end recite the place of speech as the end of sixteen.
1075.nuance: The numbers (பன்னிரண்டு, பதினாலு, சோடம் for sixteen) belong to the arrangement of the mantra and are not explained. ஆகாரம் may be the long vowel ஆ or 'form'. The verse spells the name பயிரவி; the heading has வயிரவி.

1076.reading: The fourteen at the end is Bhairavi herself; the great Shakti who rises in the lotus of the mind, as beginning, middle and end, becomes both the end and the beginning.
1076.nuance: சிந்தை கமலம், the lotus of the mind, is usually taken as the heart-lotus of meditation. The point that she is end and beginning at once is plain; what the fourteen count is not.

1077.reading: The three who come into being are absorbed in her there; Tripura goes with those of merit so that they gain light, while the ancient ones who cling to the passing elements and those who do not reach the refuge do not.
1077.nuance: ஆகின்ற மூவர் are traditionally Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra. Lines 2 and 3 (புராதரர், சாரவுழிச் சாரார்) are obscure, and the contrast between them and the புண்ணியத்தோர் is my reading of the syntax.

1078.reading: Nandi, holy and pure, becomes the goddess; with the moon that circles through the reckoned twenty-seven days, and the fire, the sun and the moon's end that were set, the one of firm mind becomes the Southern one too.
1078.nuance: திரு may be the goddess, Sri or simply holiness. The twenty-seven days are the lunar asterisms, so the verse seems to set the practice by the moon. தென்னன், the Southerner or the Pandya, is taken as a name of Siva; the whole verse is obscure.

1079.reading: For the one who stands reciting Tripura, the earth on the golden mountain praises the Southern one, holy Nandi, with his attendant, and with the Lord at the end of the mantra.
1079.nuance: பரிபிடி அந்தம் is obscure; it may name the closing of the mantra or a seat of worship. பொன்னங்கிரி, the golden mountain, is usually Meru or Kailasa.

1080.reading: Nandi who taught knows grace and declares it rightly by the way of the Veda: when the knowing joined with the moon runs twenty-seven days, the trident of radiant Bhairavi comes to rule.
1080.nuance: The twenty-seven days again tie the practice to the lunar month. The trident's 'ruling' is commonly taken as her protection or possession of the practiser; the verse does not say which.

1081.reading: The trident-bearer who holds trident and skull has a fourth pair of hands holding noose and goad; she is the gentle one who stands as the upper limb of the form that Vishnu and Brahma could not know.
1081.nuance: The form Vishnu and Brahma could not know is Siva's column of fire; the goddess is placed as part of it (மேல்அங்கம்), which is read as her being half of Siva's body. நாலாங் கரம் can also be read as four hands in all.

1082.reading: The gentle vine-like one, knower of the kalas and of wisdom, jewelled and of the colour of the kinjuka flower, has a holy body like stone and wears garments of many kinds and many gems.
1082.nuance: கிஞ்சுகம், the palasa flower, makes her red. விடமி (she of poison?) is obscure, and line 3 is corrupt in the text, so 'like stone' is a guess at கல்லியல் ஒப்பது.

1083.reading: Her crown has many gems, like ten million moons; she wears gem earrings and has a doe's eyes; her good gem-eyes are sun and moon, and she brims with golden gems and with fire.
1083.nuance: சூரிய சோம நயனம் with வன்னி gives the three eyes of sun, moon and fire, the third eye shared with Siva. The verse is a description for visualising her, as 1082 is.

1084.reading: Within the eight petals of the full-blown flower there is a noble lady; there are eight maidens there, and the sixty-four women spread around came near and saw the Shakti.
1084.nuance: The eight-petalled lotus is a worship diagram. The eight maidens and sixty-four women are traditionally her attendant powers (the eight mothers and sixty-four yoginis), but the verse names none of them.

1085.reading: With anklets, bangles, conch and discus seen on her, the yogini of the eight directions, the Goddess, Parashakti, the gracious one who bears the cosmos and the eight directions, is worshipped within the lotus.
1085.nuance: Conch and discus are Vishnu's emblems; here they are hers, as the verses after say that the gods are forms of her.

1086.reading: With worship, scent, adorned flowers and great banners, in contemplation the sound of the five comes and speaks; in the gem-mantra yoga that needs no dwelling, see Tripura shining in her radiance.
1086.nuance: பஞ்சத்து ஒலி, the sound of the five, may be the five-syllable mantra or five inner sounds. வாசம் இலாத may mean without scent or without abode. The verse moves from outer worship to inner hearing and sight.

1087.reading: The many gods one sees are each different, just as the many ornaments worn appear many though they are gold; see that the Mistress is the good cause of Siva, Brahma and Vishnu whom people honour.
1087.nuance: The gold and ornaments image is the classic one for one substance in many forms. Here even Siva is among the forms caused by her, which the hymn later balances by calling him her husband and the light (1119, 1123).

1088.reading: The Karani mantra recited in the lotus, joined with filling, holding and emptying the breath, and Narani, set in the middle as Nandi taught, are the end of the Vedic books too.
1088.nuance: பூரண கும்ப விரேசம் is read as பூரகம், கும்பகம், இரேசகம், the three phases of breath control. காரணி and நாரணி are names of the goddess. ஆரண வேதநூல் அந்தம் may simply mean Vedanta.

1089.reading: From the end, the middle finger, to the beginning, the little finger, recite reversing the order in which it came; understand clearly the start of fine Tamil and worship: Nandi taught this as new.
1089.nuance: The verse describes placing the mantra's syllables on the fingers. செந்தமிழ் ஆதி may be the Tamil letters from அ, or Tamil as the first speech. நவம் can mean new or nine; 1090 begins with நவசத்தி, the nine Shaktis.

1090.reading: When the nine Shaktis spoken of are finished one by one, counting the long order of the zodiac signs, Nandi, who earlier spoke of the eight, set them in order and fixed rule and observance.
1090.nuance: பிரைச்சதம் எட்டு is obscure. நியதி நியமம் may be the rule of practice or the second limb of yoga. The verse seems to tie the nine powers to the cycle of signs.

1091.reading: She of garlanded tresses and merciful eyes, the young vine who stands within and scatters the darkness of the night: see the fine smoke rise inside the great flame of the fire rite, mingle and return with nectar.
1091.nuance: அழுதொடு is read as அமுதொடு, with nectar; as written it could mean 'with weeping'. ஏமத்து இருள் may be the darkness of night or of delusion. The fire rite may be outward or the inner fire.

1092.reading: Seeing the heart mantra, say 'nama' in honour; upon the head the oblation set in the middle; and the end said to be worn in the middle is for the topknot.
1092.nuance: The verse runs through the limbs of the mantra placed on the body (அங்க நியாசம்): heart with namah, head with the oblation word (ஆகுதி, svaha), topknot (சிகை) with its ending. Lines 3 and 4 are compressed and the endings are the tradition's, not named.

1093.reading: With the armour at the end of the topknot, then turning to look at the limb that stands as enemy, and then the eye, the mudras, the trident, and the yoni in its kind can be formed.
1093.nuance: கவசம் (armour), நேத்திரம் (eye) and the limb 'that stands as enemy' continue the limbs of the mantra; the last is commonly taken as the weapon (astra). Then the hand-seals: trident and yoni.

1094.reading: Crossing the two little fingers, joining them, pointing and holding with the ring fingers, pressing them together and setting the two thumbs within the middle, speak.
1094.nuance: A hand-seal described finger by finger, taken as the yoni mudra of 1093. வருத்தம் இரண்டும் is obscure, and which fingers அணிவிரல் and பெருத்த விரல் are is the usual reading, not certain.

1095.reading: Recite the spoken mantra dividing it by its sounds; taking the sa-letter first without hesitation, for the teaching of the breath and prana, take it with the shrinking bindu and call.
1095.nuance: சகாரம் and the bindu (the nasal dot) build a seed-syllable. இராகம் may be tone or the mantra's parts; வாசி is the breath. The exact syllable is not recoverable from the verse.

1096.reading: With the soul that was called and prana first, with the spread 'sau' and the ya-letter made, with maya joined and the wide conch mudra, the Goddess shone in the middle.
1096.nuance: சவ் and யகாரம் are seed-letters; சவ் is the familiar bija of Tripura worship. The verse ends the rite with the goddess present in the middle of the diagram or of the body.

1097.reading: Bhairavi who stands, the dark one, the night-walker, the Lady who goes in grace into the heart where one and two have joined, for the Lord of the gods: seek her, proclaiming her in the world she graces well.
1097.nuance: நீலி and நிசாசரி are fierce names. ஒன்றும் இரண்டும் ஒருங்கிய உள்ளம் may be the heart where the soul and the Lord, or Siva and Shakti, are one. From here the chapter becomes a hymn.

1098.reading: The first mother stands with her power as the Veda that was proclaimed, the moving and unmoving, the five elements, the four directions, the three-eyed one, darkness and open space, the many lives that appear, the light and Parapara.
1098.nuance: A list identifying her with everything, from scripture and the elements to Siva himself (முக்கண்ணி can be she of three eyes) and the supreme (பராபரை).

1099.reading: If one recites and realises primal Bhairavi abiding at the virgin's shore, body and life become the Lord, births in this foolish world are destroyed, and an unending form becomes one.
1099.nuance: கன்னித்துறை is often taken as Kanyakumari, where the goddess is a virgin; it may also be an inner place. உடலுயிர் ஈசனாம் can mean body and soul become the Lord, or that the Lord is the soul of the body.

1100.reading: The lovely girl, with eyes like the blue water-lily under curving brows, Ananda Sundari, the sweet nectar that delights, revealed the Siva above.
1100.nuance: Shakti reveals Siva: the hymn's recurring claim that the way to Siva is through her. மேலைச் சிவம் may be Siva beyond, or Siva at the crown of the head.

1101.reading: She revealed, made me know the fruit, made it clear within my mind, made me rejoice, made the rayed light shine, and took me so that I was saved.
1101.nuance: Five lines of the causative -வித்து (made to) give a sequence: revelation, understanding, clarity, joy, light, rescue. The poet speaks in the first person, as through most of the hymn.

1102.reading: She took countless millions of forms, she saw the garlands in the eye of the sixty-four kalas, and she opened the three wide rays above: the fine woman who stands above the head.
1102.nuance: எண்ணெண் கலை are the sixty-four arts or kalas. The three rays are traditionally sun, moon and fire. தண்டலை may be the top of the spine (தண்டு) or a grove; the yogic sense is likely but not fixed.

1103.reading: Stand and praise slowly and bow to the fine woman, the leader of austerity, Manonmani who looks on delusion; once you have bowed, cruel births will not come again.
1103.nuance: மையலை நோக்கும் can be 'who looks upon (and so ends) delusion'. Bowing as the end of births is an old pattern; here it is to the goddess.

1104.reading: She of bamboo-like shoulders, with tresses set with fragrant soft flowers, wearing the young crescent, the beautiful trident-bearer with the pure crown of hair, has sat sweetly in my heart.
1104.nuance: The crescent and trident are Siva's marks, worn by her. The verse turns from description to her dwelling in the poet, which the following verses develop.

1105.reading: The maiden who dwells in the sweet southern corner, the sole lady and leader herself, set me apart, brought me to refuge, filled me, and stands seeking my heart.
1105.nuance: தென் மூலை is the southern corner, perhaps Kanyakumari again (1099); மூலை may also hint at மூலம், the base of the spine. தனிப்படுவித்தனள் may be 'made me single' or 'made me unique'.

1106.reading: The maiden of the clan, joined with wisdom where the three channels rise through the middle, sleeps within, the fresh gold anklets on her small feet sounding.
1106.nuance: The sleeping maiden in the middle of the three channels is traditionally kundalini, coiled until woken. The verse does not use the word; குலக்கன்னி may echo kula, the base. Why she sleeps while the channels rise is unclear.

1107.reading: While I slept, Manonmani came, embraced my neck with her jingling bangled arms, spat her shining betel into my mouth, said 'Do not sleep, sir', and gave me the means.
1107.nuance: உறங்கும் அளவில் may be the poet's sleep or follow on from her sleep in 1106. Giving her chewed betel is an image of intimate grace known from devotional legend. உபாயம், the means, is taken as the yogic method of waking.

1108.reading: The one who gives the means rooted out all danger from my heart, made love grow, held craving down inside the whirl that lights the breath, and said 'Fear not'.
1108.nuance: சுவா is read as the breath (சுவாசம்), and சுழி as a whirl or centre in the body; both are uncertain. அஞ்சல் is the gesture and word of reassurance.

1109.reading: They say that she of sweet speech, the girl of rare austerity, of true and gentle words, richly jewelled, is the goddess who gives sweet words to those who praise her red feet, thinking her their refuge.
1109.nuance: The verse repeats sweet speech in her and as her gift. என்றாரே, 'they said', presents it as the word of others, not the poet's own.

1110.reading: The girl of rare austerity who is dear life, Karani and Narani within the dark-tressed one, the fierce one who withdraws towns, lives and worlds, plays in my heart.
1110.nuance: ஒடுக்கிடும், withdraws, gives her the act of dissolution, one of the five acts. Fierce and tender names sit together through the hymn.

1111.reading: The lovely maiden who played shone in my heart, joined it for many days, moved there and came to know it, and is the one at the head of the kalas who mingles within the crown of the head.
1111.nuance: The movement from heart to crown (உச்சி) suggests the yogic rising of Shakti. கலைத்தலை may be the summit of the kalas or of the moon's digits at the head.

1112.reading: In the eye of the forehead that has one eye, at the head of the kalas, the breasted woman stays embraced; looking to the discernment at the bow's head, the swaying flower-branch stayed there.
1112.nuance: The forehead eye and சிலைத்தலை (the head of the bow, the brow) point to the place between the eyebrows. Whom she embraces is left unsaid; it is usually taken as Siva.

1113.reading: The jewelled one sat, entering my heart; she entered the four fingers' space and embraced, joined with the perfected pillar and became one with it, and the primal one attained rare austerity.
1113.nuance: தாணு, the pillar, is a name of Siva. நால்விரல் may be a measure of four finger-breadths in the body. Line 3 is corrupt in the text; ஒன்றி is read.

1114.reading: The beginning and the beginningless, the causeless and the cause, the light of light, Sundari of supreme bliss, the woman, samadhi, Manonmani, the auspicious one, recited, joined my heart.
1114.nuance: A string of names held together in paradox: beginning and beginningless, causeless and cause. Line 3 recurs in 1120, and line 1 in 1124.

1115.reading: The jewelled one joined my heart and raised it; she desired there the words 'namasiva'; she grasps the state that knows Brahma; she moved and cut away all my other babble.
1115.nuance: நமசிவ is the five-syllable mantra. அயன்தனை ஓரும் பதம் is obscure: perhaps the word that knows the creator, or the state beyond him. பிதற்று, babble, is the idle speech the mantra replaces. மேலி is probably மேவி.

1116.reading: Foolish people babbled and passed away; before those whose effort is complete stand the first mother who grants grace, her three fish-bright eyes, her red mouth that speaks, and the gracious look of her face.
1116.nuance: முயற்றியின் முற்றி may mean 'when effort is complete' or 'complete in effort'. கம்பலை (clamour, sound) with செவ்வாய் is unusual.

1117.reading: Within the three, mind, heart and breast, a child's path was born as it was spoken; in the womb of the bountiful Tiru, the virgin is the intent of the stealthy light of Mahamaya.
1117.nuance: The verse is obscure throughout. உள்ளம், இதயம், நெஞ்சம் are three inner seats. கள்ள ஒளி, stealthy light, fits maya as what both shows and hides. It prepares the virgin mother of 1118.

1118.reading: The virgin, and the virgin undone, the beloved of pure words, bore the five; the lords of the well-made books are there too: what is this? This maya is darkness itself.
1118.nuance: The paradox of a virgin who is mother. ஐவர, the five, are traditionally the five gods of the five acts. Line 2 is corrupt in the text. Whether 'this maya is darkness' rebukes those who cannot grasp the paradox or names her as maya is open.

1119.reading: Darkness is Shakti and light is our Lord; the substance is the joy in the enjoyment of the meritorious; if one, in clarity, thinks of the mind as god, our primal Lord grants grace.
1119.nuance: Shakti as darkness and Siva as light can be read as concealing and revealing, two of the five acts. Line 4 may also be read 'if one thinks of god with a clear mind'.

1120.reading: Parashakti, who is beginning and beginningless, the green-bangled one dwelling above as Parapara and as the half, the woman, samadhi, Manonmani, the auspicious one, blossomed together in my reciting heart.
1120.nuance: பாதி, the half, is her place as the left half of Siva. The verse repeats 1114 nearly line for line but ends 'blossomed' (முகிழ்த்தாள்) instead of 'joined'.

1121.reading: As it is recited, people do not know that the highest of the kalas is the Veda from the beginning; the mistress of the cow declared that he stands as caste, difference and the tattvas, and is the first.
1121.nuance: ஆவின் கிழத்தி, mistress of the cow, also reads as mistress of souls, since ஆ (cow) and pasu are one word; 1122 ties her to Tiruvavaduturai. Who 'stands as caste and difference' is unclear; perhaps the Lord, perhaps her.

1122.reading: The mistress of the cow, the mistress of the cool shore of good Avaduturai, the mistress of speech whom they praise, the mistress of the gods, Siva's woman who is Tiru, the mistress who abides, drove out my deeds.
1122.nuance: ஆவடுதண்துறை is Tiruvavaduturai, where tradition places Tirumular's life and his entering the cowherd's body; the cow names gain local weight here. நாவின் கிழத்தி may be Sarasvati as a form of her.

1123.reading: Abiding as the inner light in the hearts of those whose deeds are driven out, she stands as the tattva for all who reach her; the jewelled one who made me her servant becomes the beginningless too, so that one may see the Lord her husband.
1123.nuance: Picking up வினைகடிந்தாள் from 1122. Line 4 is compressed: she is the way to seeing Siva, and is called beginningless as he is.

1124.reading: The beginning and the beginningless, the causeless and the cause, she searched out the Veda; the light that stood for the Vedic ones, standing in the form of a lone flame, is Parapara, the half, the first of the twelve.
1124.nuance: பன்னிரண்டு ஆதி returns to the twelve kalas of the opening verse, closing the chapter as a ring. Line 1 repeats 1114.

links.note: The chapter opens with Bhairavi as the first of twelve kalas, a count in a mantra, and closes with her as the first of the twelve again; by the end the count is a name of the goddess praised as beginning and beginningless.
1106 leaves the maiden asleep in the middle channel; 1107 has Manonmani come in sleep, embrace and say 'do not sleep'. Read together, the waking is hers and his at once.
1118 ends calling maya darkness; 1119 opens by saying darkness is Shakti and light is the Lord, so the darkness is not rejected but given to her as one of two powers.
1115 says she cut away the poet's babble with the five-syllable mantra; 1116 says the foolish who went on babbling passed away, while she stands before those whose effort is complete.
The same line of names (woman, samadhi, Manonmani, the auspicious one) in both; in 1114 she joins the heart, in 1120 she blossoms in it, a refrain that marks the hymn's stages.
Both make reaching or bowing at the divine feet the end of births: the Kural's sea of births, Tirumular's cruel births. Tirumular gives it to the goddess, the Kural to the unnamed Lord.
The Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who praise the Lord truly; 1122 praises her by name after name and ends that she drove out the poet's deeds.

source_issues: 1082: line 3 reads ஒப்fபது, with a stray Latin f; the line is probably corrupt beyond that.
1113: line 3 reads ஒன்fறி, a stray f for ஒன்றி.
1118: line 2 reads துன்னியங fகைவரை, a stray f; probably துன்னியங்கு ஐவரை.
1101: line 4 reads உய்ய்க்கொண்டாளே, probably a misprint for உய்யக்கொண்டாளே.
1115: line 1 reads மேலி, probably a misprint for மேவி (cf. 1113 மேவி).
1077 lines 2 and 3, 1079 line 3 (பரிபிடி அந்தம்), 1090 line 3 (பிரைச்சதம்) and 1117 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1075 spells the goddess பயிரவி; the chapter heading and later verses have வயிரவி.
